title: Cofibration local equivalences detected by strict mapping spaces
statement: Use the model, simplicial-model and derived mapping-space conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a left proper simplicial model category: pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence. Let $\mathcal Z$ be any class of fibrant objects closed under weak equivalences between fibrant objects. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$, write $f\in W_{\mathcal Z}$ if $\operatorname{Map}^h(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(X,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $Z\in\mathcal Z$. For every cofibration $i:A\to B$, with no cofibrancy assumption on $A$ or $B$, one has $i\in W_{\mathcal Z}$ if and only if $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(B,Z)\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Z)$ is a trivial Kan fibration for every $Z\in\mathcal Z$. A trivial Kan fibration means a map having the right lifting property against all boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, including $n=0$, as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Lemma A.3.7.1, printed pp. 906-908 (PDF pp. 923-925), with its proof: it uses only closure of the class of local fibrant test objects under weak equivalences. No Stacks tag supplies this mapping-space detection theorem. Read online; not archived in literature/.
